card.name: Scholarly citations and philosophy quotes
card.fires_on: Small words, quote marks and word pieces inside academic citations, titles and quoted doctrine in philosophy, religion and history texts. Often just before a title or a quoted phrase begins.

modes.label: Inside reference titles
modes.description: Linking words or word pieces within a book or article title in a bibliography entry.
modes.example: Zhang Pengwei, Guo Qiyong & Wang Bei (2008). New Insight Into Mencius' Theory<< of>> the Original Goodness in Human Nature.

modes.label: Opening quote marks
modes.description: A quotation mark that opens a quoted philosophical or religious statement.
modes.example: mālā-sūtra 勝鬘經. The Mahāyāna-saṃgraha, for example, says,<< ">>All conscious objects are only constructs of consciousness

modes.label: Partway through foreign titles
modes.description: Part of a Latin or Italian name or phrase in a religious or historical citation.

card.writes: It pushes toward continuations like "vol" and away from unrelated tokens, which suggests citation volume numbers.
card.plain: It fires on small words and quote marks inside citations and quoted philosophy or religion passages.
